formats.key: deposit(bytes pubkey, bytes withdrawal_credentials, bytes signature, bytes32 deposit_data_root)
effects: The signer sends msg.value in native ETH (at least 1 ETH, a multiple of 1 gwei) to the deposit contract, and the contract keeps it.
The deposit is recorded for the validator `pubkey` on the consensus layer; it creates a new validator or tops up an existing one.
For a new validator, `withdrawal_credentials` decides who receives the stake and rewards on withdrawal (for 0x01/0x02 credentials, the address in the last 20 bytes).
The contract does not check `signature`; it only checks `deposit_data_root` against the other inputs and emits DepositEvent.
formats.shown: The intent "Stake ETH", with the validator public key and the withdrawal credentials as raw hex, and the ETH amount sent ("32 ETH").

findings.title: deposit shows withdrawal credentials only as raw 32 bytes, so the withdrawal address is not named
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit format: {"label": "Withdraw credentials", "format": "raw", "path": "#.withdrawal_credentials"}; case 0 shows "0x0100000000000000000000007e2a2fa2a064f693f0a55c5639476d913ff12d05". deposit_contract.sol deposit: require(withdrawal_credentials.length == 32). For 0x01/0x02 credentials the last 20 bytes are the withdrawal address; for 0x00 they are a BLS key hash. ERC-7730 cannot choose a format from the prefix byte.
findings.fix: Keep the raw field. Optionally add a field with path "#.withdrawal_credentials.[12:32]", format "addressName", label "Withdrawal address (0x01/0x02 credentials)", if the registry accepts the label caveat for 0x00 credentials.

findings.title: deposit to an existing validator ignores the shown withdrawal credentials; the screen cannot say so
findings.evidence: deposit_contract.sol deposit only emits DepositEvent(pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature, index); the consensus layer credits a top-up to the existing validator and keeps its old credentials. That state is not in the calldata.

findings.title: deposit hides the signature, and the contract does not verify it
findings.evidence: descriptor: {"label": "Signature", "path": "#.signature", "visible": "never"}; deposit_contract.sol deposit only checks require(signature.length == 96) and the deposit_data_root. An invalid signature for a new validator makes the consensus layer skip the deposit, and the ETH stays in the contract. No descriptor format can verify a BLS signature.

cases.notes: 32 ETH native out to the deposit contract, shown as "Amount to deposit: 32 ETH". The reader also read the withdrawal address from the raw credentials, but was unsure whether it was theirs.

couldNotCheck: The consensus-layer handling (a top-up to an existing validator, a deposit with an invalid signature) is outside the contract source. I judged it from protocol knowledge, not from code in this directory.
